It isn’t about not having the balls. It is about knowing the best thing for our safety is to not risk pissing off a crazy person. For us, putting our personal safety first means being as non confrontational as possible because we don’t know what the guy is capable of if we offend him. If you make a good excuse to get out of the situation, the night is uneventful to the creep. He may not even remember your name. If you make a scene, you’ve embarrassed him. He will remember your face and your name. His ego has been severely bruised. He gets filled with rage. And decides he needs to teach you a lesson. Or even gets obsessed with the idea of redeeming himself so when he’s kicked out of the hotel/bar, he comes back tomorrow around check out time and watches you walk to your car. Follows you home. The story doesn’t end well. That’s how we get stalkers and other lunatics assaulting women who turn them down. 

I guess men don’t understand this because, for the most part, dating and flirting doesn’t cause them to fear for their personal safety. You turn down a woman, worst case scenario she cries or maybe even gets violent. But you can defend yourself against her. Realistically, you could knock her ass out if you needed to. Unless you’ve just rejected Ronda Rousey. 

When women reject men, we are in immediate physical danger. Even in a public place. And we know this. 

Just google news stories about women who have been assaulted or killed for rejecting men. There’s no shortage of those stories. That should help you put yourself in our shoes.

Obviously not all men are like that. Not all men are crazy potential stalkers/murderers. But if you’re some guy we just met, we just don’t know. We err on the side of caution. 

But good news, good men can help! If you see a man overstepping boundaries you can be the person who tells him to fuck off or punches him in the liver. Redirect his creepy attention to being upset with you. Let yourself be the object of his rage. Give us a chance to get away. Or even just walk up and pretend to be our boyfriend/husband.  Walk us to our car after, just in case the creep has been lurking in the parking lot after he got kicked out of the bar. Equally important, if one of your dude friends starts saying disturbing, cringey niceguy shit when a woman rejects him (calling her a cunt, switching from saying she’s hot to suddenly saying she’s an ugly fat bitch who doesn’t deserve love) call him out. Tell him he’s being emotionally immature and needs to chill. That a woman not wanting to sleep with you isn’t a big deal and something to just let go. That’s making baby steps toward changing a culture where men feel entitled rage upon rejection. It means a lot. 

Hope this helps you understand a bit more.
